Messages.Author: Tuomas Rinta
Messages.Body:
Okay, so what happens in the following situation:
Vamp A plays Dawn Operation and Superior Drawing out the Beast.
Combat is at close range.
Vamp A dodges.
Vamps B plays Claws of the Dead and strikes with them.
The methuselah controlling Vamp B plays Rotschreck.

It is clear that Vamp A is torporized, but what about Vamp B, since
Rotschreck says: Combat ends before damage is resolved. Does that mean
that the damage from DotB is not dealt, therefore Vamp B is not sent to
torpor?

Messages.Author: Jan Willem Wijsman
Messages.Body:


It would seem to me that the methuselah controlling vamp B cannot play
rötschreck, since vamp A doesn't attempt to use aggravated damage. The
damage from drawing out the beast isn't 'strike-damage', so it's
environmental. Result: vamp B goes to torpor if he/she doesn't prevent
the damage from drawing out the beast, vamp A remains unharmed.
Rötschreck cannot be played here.

Carpe noctem, JW.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Tuomas Rinta wrote:
>
> Okay, so what happens in the following situation:
> Vamp A plays Dawn Operation and Superior Drawing out the Beast.
> Combat is at close range.
> Vamp A dodges.
> Vamps B plays Claws of the Dead and strikes with them.
> The methuselah controlling Vamp B plays Rotschreck.
>
> It is clear that Vamp A is torporized, but what about Vamp B, since
> Rotschreck says: Combat ends before damage is resolved. Does that mean
> that the damage from DotB is not dealt, therefore Vamp B is not sent to
> torpor?

No. Rotschreck is referring to damage from the source in question.
DotB's damage occurs at the end of the round, whenever the rounds ends and
for whatever reason. Rotschreck ends the round before the damage from
whatever source allowed Rotschreck to be played can resolve, but, since
the round is ending, the DotB deals its damage.

--

The Meth controlling B can play Rotschreck on vamp A, since the

damage (Claws of the Dead hand strike under a Dawn Operation)
against vamp A.

Messages.Author: Tuomas Rinta

> Wait a sec, I thought rötschreck was played on a vampire who attempts to
> use aggravated damage. The way you put it here is the other way round :
> vamp b tries aggravated damage so vamp a gets the rötschreck (huh?).
> I'm sorry if I missed something, could you explain LSJ?
> On the other hand, is it possible to play rötschreck on a vampire of
> your own, i.e. let your vampire use aggravated damage to achieve this?

The way that rotschreck works, is that the methuselah controlling the
vampire that is attempting to cause agg. damage can play rotschreck, not
vica-versa.
For example:
Vamp A dodges
Vamp B plays Claws of the Dead and strikes with them
The methuselah controlling Vamp B can play Rotschreck now.
Vamp A is torporized.
And they all lived happily ever after...

Correct, eh?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Jan Willem Wijsman wrote:

> LSJ wrote:
> > The Meth controlling B can play Rotschreck on vamp A, since the
> > minion opposing vamp A (vamp B) is attempting to use aggravated
> > damage (Claws of the Dead hand strike under a Dawn Operation)
> > against vamp A.

> Wait a sec, I thought rötschreck was played on a vampire who attempts to
> use aggravated damage. The way you put it here is the other way round :
> vamp b tries aggravated damage so vamp a gets the rötschreck (huh?).
> I'm sorry if I missed something, could you explain LSJ?

Rotschreck is played on the vampire against whom a minion attempts to use
aggravated damage. Just like the card says. The old errata that switched
the role of Rotschreck was overturned on 23-JUN-1998.

> On the other hand, is it possible to play rötschreck on a vampire of
> your own, i.e. let your vampire use aggravated damage to achieve this?

Rotschreck can be played by any Methuselah (except the acting Methuselah,
since it is a Master: Out-of-turn card). The Methuselah playing it can
chose to play it on her own vampire, if she wishes. The only restriction
is that it be played on a vampire whose opponent is attempting to use
aggravated damage against him.
